chunk.title: Quick reference: water main test numbers
chunk.text: Common water main numbers (check your spec, which governs). Hydrostatic test: AWWA C600 per U.S. Pipe, at least 1.25 times working pressure at the high point and 1.5 times at the low point; some utilities use 150 psi or 1.5 times working pressure, others working pressure plus 100 psi; hold at least 2 hours. Allowable make-up water L (gallons per hour) = S x D x square root of P / 148,000; for 1,000 ft of 8 inch at 150 psi, about 0.66 gal/hr. Disinfection (AWWA C651): continuous feed at least 25 mg/L, held 24 hours, at least 10 mg/L remaining; slug at least 100 mg/L for 3 hours; tablet about 25 mg/L for 24 hours. Bac-T samples every 1,200 ft plus end and branches, two consecutive acceptable sets. Flush before chlorinating at 3.0 ft per second or more (AWWA C651-14 Sec. 4.4.2; the 2005 edition said 2.5 ft per second, which is about 390 gpm in 8 inch).
chunk.topic: Quick reference numbers
chunk.source: AWWA C600 (U.S. Pipe), utility specs, AWWA C651 summary

chunk.title: Quick reference: traffic control numbers
chunk.text: MUTCD taper formulas: 40 mph or less, L = W x S squared / 60; 45 mph or more, L = W x S (W = offset in ft, S = speed in mph). Merging taper L; shifting 1/2 L; shoulder 1/3 L; flagger one-lane two-way taper 50 to 100 ft; downstream taper 50 to 100 ft. 12 ft lane at 35 mph: 245 ft; at 55 mph: 660 ft. Advance sign spacing (national Table 6B-1; the road agency decides which streets are low or high speed, and some state manuals set it by mph): urban low speed 100 ft each; urban high speed 350 ft; rural 500 ft; freeway 1,000, 1,500, 2,640 ft. Buffer and flagger distance: 30 mph 200 ft; 35 mph 250 ft; 45 mph 360 ft; 55 mph 495 ft. Cone spacing guidance: taper, speed in mph as feet; tangent, twice that. Check your state standards and MUTCD edition.
chunk.topic: Quick reference numbers
chunk.source: FHWA MUTCD Part 6 (as summarized)

chunk.title: Advance warning sign spacing: city street, rural road, freeway (Table 6B-1, A B C)
chunk.topic: Traffic control: advance warning signs
chunk.text: Table 6B-1 gives the recommended minimum spacing for a three-sign series. A is from the taper or point of restriction back to the first sign, B is from the first sign to the second, C is from the second to the third. Urban low speed: 100 ft, 100 ft, 100 ft. Urban high speed: 350, 350, 350 ft. Rural: 500, 500, 500 ft. Expressway or freeway: 1,000 ft, 1,500 ft and 2,640 ft. The national table does not put mph numbers on low speed and high speed; the footnote says the road agency decides the speed category, and several state manuals do it by speed. Section 6B.04 adds rules of thumb: on urban streets the sign nearest the work should be about 4 to 8 times the speed limit in feet (use the high end for higher speeds); on rural highways the first sign should be 8 to 12 times the speed limit in feet, and a multi-sign series should cover 1,500 ft or more; on freeways signing may reach half a mile or more; a single sign on a low-speed residential street may be as close as 100 ft. Lengthen them for hills, curves and queues, and sign any side street that enters inside the series. ROAD WORK AHEAD should be the first sign a driver sees. The approved plan governs.
chunk.source: MUTCD 11th Edition (FHWA, Dec 2023; Rev. 1 Dec 2025), Part 6, Table 6B-1 and footnotes; Section 6B.04 paras. 3-8; Sections 6H.02, 6H.03

chunk.title: Water main disinfection and bac-T samples (AWWA C651)
chunk.text: Keep pipe clean during laying, then disinfect before connecting to the system. AWWA C651 methods: continuous feed (water with at least 25 mg/L free chlorine fills the main, held 24 hours, ending with at least 10 mg/L), tablet (25 mg/L, 24 hours, water above 41 F), or slug (100 mg/L passed through for at least 3 hours). Agency specs can be stronger (Greenbook: 50 to 100 mg/L, 24 hours, 25 mg/L residual). Flush until the water is at system chlorine levels, dechlorinate the flush water before discharge, then take bacteriological (bac-T) samples: two sets that both pass, taken as the spec says (AWWA C651-14: a second set at least 16 hours after the first, or let the main sit 16 hours and take two sets 15 minutes apart; specs written on the 2005 edition say 24 hours apart), or per the agency; all must show no coliform. Don't connect until samples pass, and resample if the main isn't put in service in time.
chunk.topic: Testing water and sewer lines
chunk.source: AWWA C651; Greenbook 306-8.9.4

chunk.title: Washington WSDOT pipe trench, bedding, backfill, and cover before equipment runs over new pipe (Section 7-08)
chunk.topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
chunk.text: Washington (WSDOT Standard Specifications M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-08, general pipe installation). Trench: remove ledge rock, boulders and stones to give at least 6 inches clearance under all parts of the pipe; keep the toe of the spoil pile at least 2 feet from the trench edge; shoring is called for in trenches 4 feet or deeper that don't meet the open-pit rules of 3-07.3(3)B (7-08.3(1)A). Bedding: compact to 90 percent of maximum density, in lifts no more than 6 inches thick along the sides of the pipe; fix line and grade by scraping or filling under the barrel, never by blocking or wedging (7-08.3(1)C). Backfill (7-08.3(3)): pipe zone compacted to 90 percent, no rocks or lumps over 3 inches; under existing pavement or roadways 6-inch layers at 95 percent; in non-traffic areas 6-inch layers at 85 percent. No tractors or heavy equipment over the pipe until backfill is 3 feet above the top of the pipe. Laying tolerance: invert within plus or minus 0.03 foot at the time of backfill, and never a reverse slope (7-08.3(2)B). Your contract's special provisions and the city's own amendments can change these numbers.
chunk.source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

chunk.title: Washington WSDOT water main: cover, backfill, pressure test, disinfection (Section 7-09)
chunk.topic: Spec books: water main installation, pressure test and disinfection
chunk.text: Washington (WSDOT M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-09, water mains). Minimum cover 36 inches over the top of the pipe; at least 1 foot over valve operating nuts. Trench width up to 1 foot above the pipe: no more than 30 inches or 1.5 times the pipe outside diameter plus 18 inches, whichever is greater. Bedding compacted to 95 percent of maximum density (7-09.3(9)); backfill to at least 95 percent, in layers of 6 inches loose or less under paved areas (7-09.3(11)). Hydrostatic test (7-09.3(23)): 150 psi above operating pressure and never less than 225 psi; sections normally no longer than 1,500 feet; pump up, stop for 15 minutes, pump back to test pressure; allowable leakage L = S x D x square root of P / 266,400 (L gallons per hour, S feet of pipe, D inches, P psi). Disinfection (7-09.3(24)): at least 50 mg/L chlorine to start, hold at least 24 hours, at least 25 mg/L left after 24 hours; flush at 2.5 feet per second or more; dechlorinate the flush water to 0.1 ppm or less and pH 6.5 to 8.5. Services 2 inch and smaller need 3 feet of cover (7-15); hydrants need a 3-foot clear radius and the sidewalk flange 2 inches above finished grade (7-14).
chunk.source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

chunk.title: Washington WSDOT sanitary sewer tests: air, water, mandrel, TV (Section 7-17)
chunk.topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
chunk.text: Washington (WSDOT M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-17.3(2), sanitary sewers). Clean and test within 15 working days after backfilling. Exfiltration: no more than 0.28 gallon per hour per inch of diameter per 100 feet, with 6 feet of head over the crown at the upper end (or over groundwater if higher), test length no more than 700 feet, no more than 16 feet of head at the low invert (7-17.3(2)B). Infiltration: 0.16 gallon per hour per inch per 100 feet when groundwater head is 2 feet or less (7-17.3(2)C). Add 0.2 gallon per hour per foot of head for each manhole in the test section (D). Low-pressure air test for pipe 30 inches and smaller: pump to 4 psig, wait at least 2 minutes, then time the drop from 3.5 to 2.5 psig; the time comes from K = 0.0111 x d squared x L and C = 0.0003918 x d x L (E); pipe that does not pass air needs four times that time (F); over 30 inches test each joint under ASTM C1103. Deflection test for thermoplastic pipe: not less than 30 days after trench backfill and compaction are complete, with a mandrel that has an odd number of legs (9 or more) and is 95 percent of the pipe's base inside diameter (G). The Engineer can require TV inspection (H).
chunk.source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

chunk.title: Ten States Standards minimum sewer slopes by pipe size (8 inch = 0.40 percent) and 2 feet per second
chunk.topic: Sewer design standards: slopes, manholes, sizes
chunk.text: Ten States Standards (Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities, 2014 edition, Section 33). A public gravity sewer carrying raw wastewater is not less than 8 inches in diameter (33.1). Sewers are designed for a mean velocity of at least 2.0 feet per second flowing full (33.41). Recommended minimum slopes, in feet per 100 feet: 8 inch 0.40; 10 inch 0.28; 12 inch 0.22; 15 inch 0.15; 18 inch 0.12; 21 inch 0.10; 24 inch 0.08 (the book's table goes on to 42 inch). Sewers 48 inches and larger are designed for at least 3.0 feet per second. Slightly flatter slopes can be allowed where the flow depth will be 0.3 of the diameter or more at design average flow (33.42). Installation (33.8): rigid pipe uses bedding Classes A, B, C or crushed stone as described in ASTM C12; flexible pipe uses embedment Classes I, II or III (ASTM D2321), carefully compacted; no debris, frozen material, large clods or stones, or organic matter in the final backfill within 2 feet of the top of the pipe (33.84). A crew does not pick the slope: lay to the plan grade, and flag it to the foreman or engineer if a plan grade is flatter than these.
chunk.source: Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities (Ten States Standards), 2014 edition, Sections 33.1-33.8 (read 2026-11-20)

chunk.title: Advance warning signs, flaggers and buffer space
chunk.text: Typical advance warning sign spacing (the MUTCD sign spacing table, distances A, B, C between signs): urban low speed 100 ft each (the road agency sets the speed category; some state manuals set it by mph); urban high speed 350 ft; rural 500 ft; expressway and freeway 1,000 / 1,500 / 2,640 ft. Leave a longitudinal buffer space ahead of the work when possible. Flaggers: trained (many states require flagger certification), wearing high-visibility apparel (ANSI 107 Class 2 or 3), using a STOP/SLOW paddle, standing where approaching drivers can see them in time and with an escape route; give the flagger a flagger-ahead sign in advance. Nighttime work needs lighting and retroreflective gear. The permit's traffic control plan governs on that job.
chunk.topic: Traffic control (work zones)
chunk.source: FHWA MUTCD 11th Edition Part 6; ANSI/ISEA 107

chunk.title: Alabama 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Alabama 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Alabama's dig law is Ala. Code Title 37, Chapter 15, with the Underground Damage Prevention Authority enforcing it. One center: Alabama 811. A 2026 rewrite (SB205) takes effect January 1, 2027; the notice and ticket-life numbers below are the same before and after. Notice: "at least two but not more than 10 working days prior to the start of the proposed excavation" (demolition or blasting: 2 working days to 30 calendar days). An excavation notice is "valid for a period of 20 working days from the proposed starting date" (demolition 30). Renew at least two working days before it expires. Premark the route or edges of the dig in white unless that would get in the way of traffic. Operators post a positive response; you may start early once all of them have. From January 1, 2027 the tolerance zone is the width of the line plus 18 inches on either side: find marked lines by noninvasive methods and keep 18 inches between any line and the cutting edge. Hit a line: notify the operator immediately.
chunk.source: Ala. Code 37-15-2, -4, -4.1, -4.2, -6, -8, -9, -10 as amended by 2026 SB205 (enrolled), effective Jan 1, 2027

chunk.title: Alaska 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Alaska 811, Alaska Digline)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Alaska's dig law is AS 42.30.400 to 42.30.490. One center: Alaska 811 (Alaska Digline). Notice: "at least two but not more than 15 working days" before digging. Remote locations: at least 10 but not more than 20 working days. The law sets no ticket expiry. The handbook says most owners treat a ticket as expired if more than 15 calendar days pass before digging starts (20 in remote places). Marks gone from weather, construction or vandalism: ask for a remark, give the old dig number, and plan on another 2 working days. Mark the dig area in white; "Black paint may be used when snow is on the ground." No digging until each line is field marked. Lines there but not located: call for a second request. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 2 feet on either side (30 inches for lines more than 10 feet deep). Hand dig or vacuum within 24 inches of a marked line. Hit a line: notify the utility and the one-call system right away; danger, clear out and call 911. Fines: $50 to $1,000 for each offense that causes or adds to damage.
chunk.source: Alaska 811 Excavator Handbook (2026) pp. 2-3, 6-8, 13-22; AS 42.30.400 to 42.30.490

chunk.title: Arizona 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Arizona 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Arizona's dig law is A.R.S. 40-360.21 to 40-360.32, enforced by the Arizona Corporation Commission. One center: Arizona 811. Mark the dig area with white lining before you call (40-360.22(C)); a person digging on a single-family home lot is excused. Operators must mark "as promptly as practicable, but not later than two working days." Working days skip Saturday, Sunday, legal holidays and the Friday after Thanksgiving. You may not start "before the location and marking are complete or the excavator is notified that marking is unnecessary." Marks are good for 15 working days from the date of marking. If work goes on, give notice at least 2 working days before they run out. Within 24 inches of a marked line, expose it carefully with hand tools and support it. Hit a line: tell the operator right away; gas or hazardous material, also call 911. Leave the hole open until the operator arrives. Fine: up to $5,000 per violation.
chunk.source: A.R.S. 40-360.21 to 40-360.28 (azleg.gov; statute copy in Southwest Gas "Arizona Dig Law" booklet, rev. Aug 2017)
chunk.edition: Statute as posted on azleg.gov, read Nov 20, 2026

chunk.title: Arkansas 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Arkansas 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Arkansas's dig law is the Arkansas Underground Facilities Damage Prevention Act, Ark. Code 14-271-101 and after. One center: Arkansas 811. Notice (14-271-112): "at least two (2), but not more than ten (10), full working days before commencing" the dig. The notice is "effective for a period of twenty (20) working days from the date that the notice was given." Work not finished or marks gone: "reinitiate the notice procedure," which means calling it in again with the normal wait. The tolerance zone, white lining rule, damage steps and fine amounts were not read in this pass and are not confirmed here. Until they are: hand dig or vacuum to find any marked line before a machine works near it, and if you hit a line call the owner, and 911 if gas or liquid is escaping.
chunk.source: Ark. Code 14-271-112 (FindLaw copy, current as of Mar 28, 2024, as quoted in tests/staged/locate_round3_nov20/raw_findings.md)
chunk.edition: FindLaw copy current as of March 28, 2024
chunk.unconfirmed: tolerance zone, white lining, damage steps, fine amounts

chunk.title: California 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (USA North 811, DigAlert)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: California's dig law is Government Code 4216 to 4216.24. Two centers answer 811: USA North 811 (north and central) and DigAlert (south). Mark the dig area in white first: the law says the excavator "shall delineate the area to be excavated" before calling. Call at least 2 working days and not more than 14 calendar days before digging. Working days are Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM, not holidays, and the call day does not count. Do not dig until every operator on the ticket has marked or answered through electronic positive response. A ticket is good for 28 days from issue; renew by the end of day 28. If it expires while work goes on, stop and get a new ticket. Tolerance zone: 24 inches on each side of the field mark. Inside it, find the line with hand tools before using power equipment. Hit a line: call the operator right away; call 911 if gas or hazardous liquid is escaping; tell the 811 center within 48 hours.
chunk.source: Cal. Gov. Code 4216, 4216.2, 4216.3, 4216.4, 4216.6 (FindLaw copy, current as of Jan 1, 2026)

chunk.title: Colorado 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Colorado 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Colorado's dig law is C.R.S. 9-1.5-101 to 9-1.5-108, with the Underground Damage Prevention Safety Commission hearing violations. One center: Colorado 811. Notice: "at least two (2) full business days prior to any excavation," not counting the call day. Marks are good for 30 days from the ticket's due date, or until you can't see them, whichever is first. To go on, notify Colorado 811 at least 2 business days before the 30 days end; once it has run out you need a new ticket. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 18 inches on each side. Use non-destructive digging there (hand or vacuum). Check that every member on the ticket has posted a positive response before you dig. If one has not by the locate-by date, send an Excavator Re-Notification first. Hit a line: stop, notify 811 and the operator right away; gas release, clear the area and call 911.
chunk.source: Colorado 811 Excavator Handbook (last update Nov 2022) pp. 5-23, 27-45; C.R.S. 9-1.5-103

chunk.title: Connecticut 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Call Before You Dig)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Connecticut's dig law is Conn. Gen. Stat. 16-345 to 16-359 with regulations R.C.S.A. 16-345-1 to 16-345-9. The Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA) oversees and enforces it. Call 811 (Call Before You Dig, CBYD). Notice: "at least two full days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, but not more than thirty (30) days" before digging. The app's table gives a 30-day ticket life from the regulation; that and the hand-dig distance were not on the page read today and are not confirmed here. Forgetting to call is not an emergency. An emergency excavation is one "necessary to correct an emergency involving danger to life, health, or property." Hit or touch a line: "Immediately and directly report the contact or damage to the affected public utility." For a gas escape or other danger, also alert emergency personnel (911) and keep people away. Violations can bring a civil penalty from PURA; the amount was not on the page.
chunk.source: R.C.S.A. 16-345-1 to 16-345-9 as described on the PURA "CBYD Current Provisions" page
chunk.unconfirmed: ticket life, tolerance zone and penalty amounts

chunk.title: Delaware 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Miss Utility of Delmarva)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Delaware's dig law is the Underground Utility Damage Prevention and Safety Act, 26 Del. C. chapter 8, enforced by the Public Service Commission. Call 811 (Miss Utility of Delmarva). Notice: "not less than 3 business days, but no more than 12 business days" before work begins. A ticket "is valid for 12 business days after the day on which the ticket is transmitted." "On the thirteenth day, the ticket will expire, and an update, remark, or new excavation ticket shall be required." "No excavation may begin until a positive response code of clear or no conflict or marked is received." Tolerance zone: 24 inches from the outside wall or edge of the line. No mechanized equipment in it except to remove pavement; vacuum excavation is allowed; hand dig. White line marking is highly recommended when the exact location can't be given. Hit a line: report it to the owner immediately; dangerous gas or liquid escaping, call 911.
chunk.source: 26 Del. C. 802, 803, 805, 806, 808, 810 (Underground Utility Damage Prevention and Safety Act; through 85 Del. Laws c. 345)
chunk.edition: Delaware Code online, through 85 Del. Laws c. 345

chunk.title: District of Columbia 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: The District of Columbia's dig law is D.C. Code Title 34, Chapter 27. Call 811 (District One Call). Notice: at least 96 hours and not more than 10 days before work begins, not counting Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays. A notice is good for 15 days, not counting weekends and legal holidays. Three days before that ends, or when marks can't be read, ask the one-call center for a re-mark; re-marking is done within 48 hours. No digging until the one-call center confirms the operators have answered (they have 72 hours). Marks are within 2 feet of the outermost part of the line. Within 18 inches of it, expose the line by hand digging. Hit a line: notify the operator immediately; gas or liquid release, also 911. No backfill over a damaged line without the operator's permission. Fines: $2,500 first violation, $5,000 second, $10,000 third or later.
chunk.edition: D.C. Code online, through D.C. Law 23-186 (2021)

chunk.title: Florida 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Sunshine 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Florida's dig law is chapter 556, the Underground Facility Damage Prevention and Safety Act. One center: Sunshine 811. Notice: "not less than 2 full business days before beginning any excavation" (10 full business days for underwater work). A ticket is valid for 30 calendar days. Not finished: give another notice for the part still to dig. Tolerance zone: 24 inches from the outer edge of either side of the marked line. Inside it, "use increased caution": hand dig, pothole, soft dig or vacuum. You must check the positive responses before you dig. Pre-mark in white when the site can't otherwise be identified. Hit a line: "immediately notify the member operator"; if gas or a hazardous substance escapes, call 911. Citations are $500 plus court costs, $2,500 for hazardous material pipelines.

chunk.title: Georgia 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Georgia 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Georgia's dig law is the Georgia Underground Facility Protection Act, O.C.G.A. 25-9, enforced by the Public Service Commission. One center: Georgia 811. Notice: the notice period starts at 7 AM on the first business day after Georgia 811 gets your request and runs at least 2 business days, so a Monday request is good to dig Thursday at 7 AM. A request after 4:30 PM counts as the next business day. You may start early only if every owner has already answered clear or marked. Check the Positive Response Information System (PRIS) before digging. A locate request is good for 30 calendar days. Georgia 811 allows a normal ticket to be updated two times (90 days); each update is a new ticket number. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 18 inches on either side. Hit a line: stop, notify Georgia 811 and the owner; gas or hazardous liquid, call 911. Fines up to $10,000 per violation.

chunk.title: Hawaii 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Hawaii One Call Center)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Hawaii's dig law is HRS chapter 269E, under the Public Utilities Commission. One center: the Hawaii One Call Center (811). Notice: "at least five working days but not more than twenty-eight calendar days prior to commencing excavation," except in an emergency. The center issues an inquiry identification number that "shall remain valid for not more than twenty-eight calendar days from the date of issuance." Ask to revalidate it before it expires; you must hold a valid number for the whole time you are digging. No notice is needed on private property owned only by the excavator where no operator has lines. The center notifies the operators the same day. The tolerance zone, hand-dig rule, damage steps and fine amounts are in other sections (269E-12 to 269E-14) that were not read in this pass and are not confirmed here.
chunk.source: HRS 269E-7 (capitol.hawaii.gov)
chunk.edition: HRS current edition online, read Nov 20, 2026
chunk.unconfirmed: tolerance zone, damage steps, fine amounts

chunk.title: Idaho 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Idaho's dig law is Idaho Code Title 55, Chapter 22, with the Damage Prevention Board hearing violations. Three centers answer 811: Dig Safe North Idaho 811 (Boundary, Bonner, Kootenai counties), North Idaho 811 (Benewah, Shoshone) and Digline (all other counties). Notice: "not less than two (2) business days nor more than ten (10) business days before the scheduled date." Marks you keep up are good for "no longer than four (4) consecutive weeks following the date of notification." If work has not started within three weeks, give notice again. An Update request extends an active ticket. Pre-mark the path of the dig in white paint. Do not dig "until all known facilities have been marked." Marks missing: send a Second request. Tolerance zone: 24 inches from the outside edges of the line; find the line by hand digging there. Hit a line: notify the owner and the one-number service; danger, call 911 and clear the area. Report the damage to the Board.
chunk.source: Idaho Guide to Safe Digging 2026-27 (Damage Prevention Board, DOPL) pp. 4, 7, 9-12, 15-20, 29-36; Idaho Code 55-2201 to 55-2212
chunk.edition: 2026-27 guide; statutes and rules in it current as of July 1, 2024

chunk.title: Illinois 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (JULIE; Chicago is separate)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Illinois's dig law is the Underground Utility Facilities Damage Prevention Act, 220 ILCS 50, rewritten effective January 1, 2025 and enforced by the Illinois Commerce Commission. JULIE is the one-call center everywhere outside the City of Chicago; Chicago runs its own system (811 Chicago). Notice: "not less than 2 days but no more than 10 days in advance." A "day" skips Saturdays, Sundays, JULIE holidays and the day of the notice. A normal notice is good for 25 days from the first request. An extension can be asked for from day 20 and adds 25 days. Pre-mark the dig area in white (black when there is snow on the ground). Since January 1, 2026: confirm every notified operator has posted a positive response before you dig. Tolerance zone: one and one-half feet (18 inches) on either side of the outside edge of the marked line. Hit a line: notify the owner and JULIE right away; gas or hazardous material escaping, call 911.

chunk.title: Iowa 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Iowa One Call)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Iowa's dig law is Iowa Code chapter 480; the Attorney General enforces it. One center: Iowa One Call. Notice: "at least forty-eight hours prior to the commencement" of digging, not counting the notice day, weekends and legal holidays. A ticket is "valid for twenty-five (25) calendar days beginning on the day the forty-eight-hour period concludes." There is no renewal: for a longer job, request a new locate ticket before the old one runs out. You can't dig on another excavator's ticket. Use white paint, flags or stakes to show the dig area unless it is clearly defined or you used electronic white-lining. Operators must post a positive response within the 48 hours. Check the Electronic Positive Response System before starting; if one is missing, contact the operator or Iowa One Call. Tolerance zone: 18 inches on either side of the line. Hand-dig test holes there; no machinery other than accepted methods such as vacuum excavation. Hit a line: tell the operator as soon as practical and do not backfill until it has looked; gas or liquid escaping, call 911.
chunk.source: Iowa One Call Excavator Manual (July 2024) pp. 2, 12-19, 32-46, 54-56; Iowa Code ch. 480

chunk.title: Kansas 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Kansas 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Kansas's dig law is the Kansas Underground Utility Damage Prevention Act, K.S.A. 66-1801 to 66-1816, enforced by the Kansas Corporation Commission. One center: Kansas 811. Notice: "at least two full working days but not more than 20 calendar days before the scheduled excavation start date." The notice, or any update, is "valid for 20 calendar days after the excavation start date" (changed from 15 days on January 1, 2024). Ticket only what you can reasonably finish in that time. To go on, update the notice. Do not make repeated remark requests unless the cause was out of your control; the Commission has warned of fines for needless updates. Whiteline the dig area when the operator asks for it. Pre-engineered and permitted projects still need the notice before digging starts. The tolerance zone (24 inches in K.S.A. 66-1802) and fine amounts were not re-read today and are not confirmed here.
chunk.source: K.S.A. 66-1804 (ksrevisor.gov, as amended eff. Jan 1, 2024)

chunk.title: Kentucky 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Kentucky 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Kentucky's dig law is the Underground Facility Damage Prevention Act, KRS 367.4901 to 367.4917. One center: Kentucky 811. Notice: "not less than two (2) full working days nor more than ten (10) full working days prior to commencing work." "Locate requests are valid for twenty-one (21) calendar days from the day of the initial request." Ask for remarking two working days before each 21-day period ends, or sooner if the marks are gone or the plan changes. One request may not cover more than 5,000 feet unless you and the operator agree. Mark the edges of the dig yourself when an operator asks or the area can't be described. Operator did not respond in time: "the excavator shall submit a second notice." If there is still nothing one working day later, an excavator who followed the law is not liable for damage to lines that would have been located (not true for certain gas and hazardous liquid pipelines). Inside the tolerance zone, "hand-dig or use nonintrusive means." Machines are allowed for pavement, rock, and material more than 12 inches in any direction from the located line, with a watcher. Hit a line: stop and notify the operators; flammable, toxic or corrosive escape, call 911.
chunk.source: KRS 367.4911 (Justia copy, effective Jan 1, 2022)

chunk.title: Louisiana 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Louisiana 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Louisiana's dig law is the Underground Utilities and Facilities Damage Prevention Law, R.S. 40:1749.11 to 1749.27 (amended effective August 1, 2026). One center: Louisiana 811. Notice (R.S. 40:1749.13): at least 48 hours and not more than 120 hours ahead, not counting weekends and holidays; the wait runs from 7:00 a.m. on the next working day after you call. Marks are good "as long as visible, but not longer than twenty calendar days, including weekends and holidays," from the mark-by time. Marks gone or work not done in time: give another notice to the center. Forestry, farm and marine digging: up to 30 calendar days. A notice designated a large project with a written agreement: 90 calendar days. Operators give a positive response through the center by the mark-by time; bad weather extends it. The marked location is the width of the line "plus eighteen inches on either side." Marks use the APWA color code. An excavator who called and followed the law is immune from civil liability to an operator that did not join the center or did not mark, unless the excavator was negligent. Fine amounts and the damage steps were not confirmed in this pass.
chunk.source: La. R.S. 40:1749.14 (legis.la.gov; last amended by Acts 2026, No. 902, eff. Aug 1, 2026); R.S. 40:1749.13
chunk.unconfirmed: fine amounts and damage reporting steps

chunk.title: Maine 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Dig Safe)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Maine uses Dig Safe as its one-call center (call 811); the Public Utilities Commission enforces the state's Dig Safe law. Pre-mark the dig area in white (paint, flags, stakes or whiskers), then call at least 72 hours ahead, not counting weekends and holidays, and not more than 30 days ahead. Ticket life: tickets expire every 60 days. In every Dig Safe state a ticket expires if digging does not start within 30 days. Renew with at least 72 hours' notice (weekends and holidays not counted) so there is no gap; if the scope of work changes, get a new ticket instead. Whether a renewal prints a new number is not confirmed. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 18 inches on each side. Hand dig or use vacuum equipment there; no machines until the line is verified. Power equipment may remove pavement only to the depth of the pavement. Dig Safe only notifies its members. Call non-member owners (often town water and sewer) yourself. Maine also has its own damage prevention statute, 23 M.R.S. 3360-A.
chunk.source: Dig Safe Excavator Manual (version Aug 2025; laws table updated 6/5/25) pp. 4-5, 9, 11, 14-19, 25-27, 31

chunk.title: Maryland 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Miss Utility)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Maryland's dig law is Public Utilities Article Title 12, Subtitle 1, enforced by the Maryland Underground Facilities Damage Prevention Authority. Call 811 (Miss Utility). Pick a start date "not sooner than 3 business days after the ticket is initiated" and not later than 12 business days after. Business days are Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM, not holidays; a ticket taken after hours counts from the next business morning. "A ticket is valid for 12 business days after the selected start work date." If the work won't be done in that time, "repeat the notification" the same way as the first. Ticket Check (positive response) is mandatory for owner-members. Check it before digging: 866-821-4226 or online. Code 11 (critical facilities) is not a go-ahead. Emergency tickets: owners respond within two hours. The 18-inch hand-dig rule and fine amounts come from the statute, were not re-read today and are not confirmed here.
chunk.source: Md. Code, Public Utilities 12-124, 12-125 (FindLaw); Miss Utility Maryland page (missutility.net/maryland)
chunk.edition: Miss Utility page as posted Nov 20, 2026
chunk.unconfirmed: 18-inch rule and fine amounts not re-read

chunk.title: Michigan 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (MISS DIG 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Michigan's dig law is the MISS DIG Underground Facility Damage Prevention and Safety Act, 2013 PA 174 (MCL 460.721 to 460.733), enforced by the Michigan Public Service Commission. One center: MISS DIG 811. Notice: "at least 72 hours, but not more than 14 calendar days, before the start." Hours on non-business days do not count. A ticket is "valid for 21 days from the start date," or 180 days when the notice says the work will take longer. Past that, or if digging did not start in time, get a new ticket. Caution zone: 48 inches on either side of the marks. Before digging there, expose every marked line by soft excavation (hand or vacuum). Check positive response. No response on a ticket is a reason to stop near there and give additional notice. Hit a line: notify the owner right away; gas or liquid escaping or danger to life, call 911.
chunk.edition: MCL compilation complete through PA 91 of 2026

chunk.title: Minnesota 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Gopher State One Call)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Minnesota's dig law is Minn. Stat. chapter 216D, enforced by the Minnesota Office of Pipeline Safety. One center: Gopher State One Call (GSOC). Notice: at least 48 hours, not counting the day you file, weekends and holidays, and not more than 14 calendar days ahead. A ticket is good for 14 calendar days from the start date and time on it (up to six months when a marking schedule is agreed and written down). To go past 14 days, file an Update at least 48 hours (weekends and holidays not counted) before it expires; an Update gets a new ticket number and its own 48-hour wait. White marks are required: "without exception." Electronic white marks count from January 1, 2026. Check GSOC's positive response before you dig. "Not Yet Responded" and no marks: contact that operator directly. Hand dig zone: 2 feet (24 inches) from each side of the line. Hand tools or vacuum only there. Hit a line: notify the owner right away; gas or liquid escaping, call 911. Never bury a damaged line.
chunk.source: Gopher State One Call Handbook 2026 pp. 14-28, 33-46, 76, 84; Minn. Stat. ch. 216D

chunk.title: Mississippi 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Mississippi 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Mississippi's dig law is Miss. Code 77-13-1 and after, amended by HB 1191 effective July 1, 2025. One center: Mississippi 811 (MS811). Ticket life went "from 14 to 20 calendar days" for Normal, Emergency, Impending Emergency, Short Notice and Design tickets. Update at least 3 working days before a ticket expires so there is no gap. (MS811's older portal guide says an update adds 14 calendar days; whether that is now 20 is not confirmed.) The wait before digging was not on the page read and is not confirmed here: go by the dig date on your ticket. Tolerance zone: 18 inches plus one-half of the diameter of the line when the diameter is shown at the marks, measured from the outside edge of the marks. Use non-invasive methods there (hand digging, vacuum), support the line, and keep machines a safe distance away. Pre-mark in white unless you own the property and described it clearly, or you drew the dig area on the web portal map after MS811's short training. Emergency tickets: operators respond within 2 hours, and you must name a contact who will be on site. Large projects (can't be finished in 20 calendar days): optional preconstruction meeting and a signed agreement before work.
chunk.source: Mississippi 811 "2025 Excavation Law Amendments Summary" (HB 1191, effective July 1, 2025); MS811 Portal Update guide
chunk.unconfirmed: wait before digging; days added by an update

chunk.title: Missouri 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Missouri 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Missouri's dig law is the Underground Facility Safety and Damage Prevention Act, RSMo 319.010 to 319.050 (amended August 28, 2025). One center: Missouri 811. Notice: "at least two working days, but not more than ten working days, before the expected date" of starting. You may work in the area on the notice, while the marks can be seen, until the "notice of intent to excavate expiration date" printed on the ticket; the number of days is not in this section and is not confirmed here. If you can't start within ten working days, make a relocate request before digging. Marks unusable: ask the center for a remark. White lining (paint, stakes, whiskers) may be used when the site can't be clearly described. Find a line unmarked or marked wrong: notify the center; the owner must contact you or mark it correctly within two hours. Hand or soft digging "shall be used as a best practice when possible"; no hand-dig distance is given in this section. Hit a line: notify the center. Gas or hazardous liquid pipeline release: "immediately contact 911." Do not hide or repair damage without the owner's OK.
chunk.source: RSMo 319.026 (revisor.mo.gov, effective Aug 28, 2025)
chunk.unconfirmed: ticket life in days; tolerance zone

chunk.title: Montana 811: not confirmed yet: what to check with Montana 811
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Montana's dig law is Mont. Code Title 69, Chapter 4, Part 5 (underground facility protection). One center: Montana 811. None of Montana's numbers could be opened in an official source in this pass, so they are not confirmed: the wait before digging, how long a ticket lasts, the tolerance zone and the fines. Do not use another state's numbers. What to do: call 811 or go online at montana811.org before any digging, start only on or after the dig date printed on the ticket, check that every utility on the ticket has marked or cleared, and ask Montana 811 how long the ticket is good for on a long job. The federal rule applies everywhere for pipelines: use one-call first, wait for the marks, dig with care, report any pipeline damage to the operator, and call 911 if gas or hazardous liquid is released (49 CFR 196).
chunk.source: Mont. Code 69-4-501 to 69-4-530 (not opened); 49 CFR 196.103 to 196.109
chunk.edition: Not confirmed; federal rule current to Oct 22, 2026

chunk.title: Nebraska 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Nebraska 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Nebraska's dig law is the One-Call Notification System Act, Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-2301 to 76-2334. Since September 1, 2024 the State Fire Marshal investigates complaints and the Underground Excavation Safety Committee sets penalties. One center: Nebraska 811. Notice: the app's table has 2 full business days and not more than 10 business days; operators must respond "no later than two business days after receipt of a dig ticket." Do not call in an area where digging can't reasonably start "within seventeen calendar days after the ticket start date." Marks must be "within 18 inches on either side of the marking, plus one half of the width of the underground facility." Hand dig inside that strip. Hit a line: "the excavator shall immediately notify the center." Do not hide the damage or repair the line without the operator's OK. Penalties: up to $10,000 per day per event for pipeline and fiber optic violations (cap $500,000); up to $5,000 per day per event for other utilities (cap $50,000). Farm tilling and gardening for seeding are not excavation. How long a ticket lasts once digging has started was not confirmed.
chunk.source: Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-2321, 76-2323, 76-2326 and State Fire Marshal summary (One-Call Notification System Act)
chunk.edition: State Fire Marshal copy of the Act, with changes effective Sept 1, 2024
chunk.unconfirmed: ticket life after work starts; notice window not re-read

chunk.title: Nevada 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (USA North 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Nevada's dig law is NRS 455.080 to 455.180 with rules in NAC 455. One center: USA North 811. Call at least 2 working days (7 AM to 5 PM, not weekends or holidays, call day not counted) and not more than 28 calendar days before digging. Mark the dig area in white first. Wait for every operator: the handbook says excavators "are required by law to wait until all operators" have given a positive response, even if the start time on the ticket has passed. A ticket is good for 28 calendar days from the date and time of the notification. It can be extended twice, 28 days each; after that the regulation requires a new notification (NAC 455.165). That is 84 days at most on one ticket. Hand tools only within 24 inches on either side of the outside of the line. Hit a line: notify the operator right away; in an emergency also 911.
chunk.source: USA North 811 Nevada Excavation Handbook (rev. Jan 2025) pp. 3-8, 21; NRS 455.110; NAC 455.165
chunk.edition: Handbook revised January 2025; NAC 455 revised Aug 2026

chunk.title: New Jersey 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (New Jersey One Call)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: New Jersey's dig law is the Underground Facility Protection Act (N.J.S.A. 48:2-73 and after) with rules in N.J.A.C. 14:2, enforced by the Board of Public Utilities. Call 811 (New Jersey One Call). Notice: "no less than three business days before the beginning of the excavation." Start within 10 business days of the notice. The notice "shall remain valid for 45 business days from the notification." Digging after that needs a new notification with the normal wait. Operators must post an electronic positive response within three business days and mark out or tell you they have no lines there. You may mark the edge of the site in white; it is optional. Marks are paint, at intervals of 25 feet or less. Hit a gas, petroleum or hazardous liquid line: "immediately call 911," then the operator, or the One-Call center at 811 if you can't reach the operator. Fines: $1,000 to $2,500 per day, up to $25,000 for a related series. The hand-dig distance (2 feet in the statute) was not confirmed in the text read.
chunk.source: N.J.A.C. 14:2-3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 4.2, 4.4, 5.2, 6.2 (BPU One-Call rules, 2021 readoption text)
chunk.edition: BPU rule text dated Oct 28, 2021 (readoption proposal)
chunk.unconfirmed: hand-dig distance; this is the 2021 proposal text, not the current code

chunk.title: New Mexico 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (NM811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: New Mexico's dig law is the Excavation Damage to Pipelines and Underground Utility Lines Act (NMSA 62-14) with rule 18.60.5 NMAC, enforced by the Public Regulation Commission's pipeline safety bureau. One center: NM811. Notice: 2 working days, not counting the day you call; operators must mark "within two full working days from the effective date of the ticket." Marks are good for 15 working days from the end of the notice period. Marks gone with no offsets: stop and ask for a relocate, only for the part still to dig, and say why. Jobs longer than 15 working days: ask for a wide area conference at least two working days ahead, write a work plan signed by all, and reaffirm the wide area ticket every 15 working days. Pre-mark in white: it shows the actual dig, not the limits of construction. Before digging, check that every operator has marked or cleared. If one has not, call for a warning locate. Within 18 inches either side of a mark, expose the line first by non-mechanical means or vacuum. Hit a line: stop, call 911 if needed, the operator and 811, secure the site, and stay until released.
chunk.source: 18.60.5 NMAC sections 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17 (Public Regulation Commission, srca.nm.gov)

chunk.title: New York 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (UDig NY, New York 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: New York's dig rules are 16 NYCRR Part 753 ("Code Rule 753") under General Business Law Article 36, enforced by the Public Service Commission. Two centers: UDig NY upstate and New York 811 for New York City and Long Island. Notice: "at least two but not more than ten working days, not including the date of the call." There is no ticket expiry date. If you put the start off by more than ten working days, give a new notice. Do not start until you have heard from "each and every operator" that its lines are marked or that it has none. Use the Automated Positive Response system where there is one. Tolerance zone: half the known diameter plus two feet on each side of the center line (two feet each side if the size is not known). Verify the line's exact location before power equipment goes in the zone; gas and liquid petroleum lines must be found with hand-dug test holes. Hit a line: tell the operator right away; gas, liquid or electric emergency, clear the area and call 911.
chunk.source: 16 NYCRR Part 753 (DPS booklet; Part 753 dated Feb 21, 2023); Gen. Bus. Law 765 (May 9, 2025)
chunk.edition: Part 753 as of February 21, 2023; booklet updated May 9, 2025

chunk.title: North Carolina 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (NC811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: North Carolina's dig law is the Underground Utility Safety and Damage Prevention Act, G.S. Chapter 87, Article 8A (amended in 2025). One center: NC811. Notice: at least 3 full working days before the start date (10 to 20 for work near underwater lines). Working days are every day but Saturday, Sunday and State holidays. A notice expires 28 calendar days after the work start date. To keep digging, give a new notice the same way; NC811 calls it an update and it gets a new ticket number. Check positive response before you dig. Tolerance zone: 24 inches on each side of the outside edge of the mark, or half the diameter plus 24 inches from the centerline when the size is known. No mechanized equipment in the zone until you can see the line. Hit a line: notify NC811 and the operator right away; gas, electricity or danger, call 911 first. No backfill until cleared.
chunk.edition: Statute as amended by Session Law 2025-21

chunk.title: North Dakota 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (North Dakota One Call)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: North Dakota's dig law is N.D.C.C. chapter 49-23. One center: North Dakota One Call (811). Notice: the handbook says "at least 48 hours (excluding weekends and holidays)" before digging. A ticket is good for 21 calendar days from the start time on it. The law says an excavator "may not use a location more than twenty-one days" after the planned dig date without arrangements with the operators; if no digging happened in the first 21 days, ask for a relocate first. After expiry, get a new ticket. There is no blanket ticket. One request covers at most three city blocks in town, or four quarter sections or five linear miles in the country. Show the site with white marking, digital white lining or project staking. Operators mark a strip two feet on either side of the line. Dig by hand within 24 inches of a located line. Emergency: call 911 first, then the utility, then the center. Hit a line: notify the operator promptly; danger, call 911 and keep people away. Knowing of damage and not reporting it, or backfilling over it, is a class A misdemeanor. Civil penalty up to $25,000. Farm work shallower than 18 inches and gardening shallower than 12 inches are not excavation.
chunk.source: N.D.C.C. 49-23-04 (Counsel Stack copy, 2026); ND One Call Locate Request Handbook (2020 copy) pp. 7-13, 21, 31-48

chunk.title: Ohio 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (OHIO811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Ohio's dig law is O.R.C. 3781.25 to 3781.38 (amended June 9, 2026); complaints go to the Underground Technical Committee at the PUCO. One center: OHIO811. Oil and gas producers answer through a separate group reached by the same call. Notice: "at least two working days, not including the day of the notification," and "not more than sixteen calendar days before commencing excavation." The law and the June 2026 manual give no ticket expiry date. Keep the ticket for the whole job and ask for a remark when marks fade. Premark the dig in white paint unless an exception applies. Check Positive Response before you go to the job; code 999 means an owner has not answered by the legal start. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 18 inches on each side. Dig there carefully, with a second person watching the bucket. Hit a line: get everyone safe, stop, notify the utility and OHIO811; anything flammable, toxic or corrosive escaping, call 911.
chunk.source: OHIO811 Excavator Manual (rev. June 2026) pp. 5-7, 10-17, 20-24, 40; O.R.C. 3781.25 to 3781.32

chunk.title: Oklahoma 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (OKIE811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Oklahoma's dig law is the Underground Facilities Damage Prevention Act, 63 O.S. 142.1 to 142.13 (last amended November 1, 2024). The Corporation Commission enforces it for oil and gas pipelines. One center: OKIE811. Notice: at least 48 hours before digging, not counting the day you call, Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays. Demolition: 7 business days. "Notice shall expire fourteen (14) calendar days from the excavation start date." To keep going, update the ticket (Extend, or Re-Mark if marks are gone) at least 4 business days before it expires; operators get 48 hours to respond. A ticket covers no more than 500 linear feet in a city or town, or one linear mile outside. White line the dig area before you call. Check positive responses before starting. Operator missing: send a Second Notice. Approximate location: a strip two feet on either side of the line. Only hand digging there until the line is exposed; machines may remove pavement only. Hit a line: notify the operator and OKIE811 immediately; gas escaping, leave and call 911. Hold the backfill until repairs are done.
chunk.source: OKIE811 Excavator Guide (Feb 2026; law text as of Nov 1, 2025) pp. 6, 10-19, 24-39; 63 O.S. 142.6

chunk.title: Oregon 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Oregon 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Oregon's dig rules are ORS 757.542 to 757.562 and OAR chapter 952, written by the Oregon Utility Notification Center (Oregon 811). Pre-mark the dig area in white, then call at least 2 full business days and not more than 10 business days before digging. Do not start until you have "received a response from each operator of underground facilities in the area." Ticket life: the Center's 2026 Addendum says the rule was changed "from 45 days to 30 days," effective January 8, 2026. Older copies of the rule and the Center's own FAQ page still say 45 calendar days, so the current number is not confirmed. Until you check with Oregon 811, plan on 30 days. Past ticket life, call in a new locate request. Tolerance zone: 24 inches around the outside of the line on all sides. Use hand tools or other non-invasive methods there. Hit a line: tell the operator right away; gas or hazardous liquid release, call 911. Don't bury it without the operator's OK.
chunk.source: OAR 952-001-0010, -0050, -0070, -0090 (Oregon Utility Notification Center); 2026 Addendum to the Oregon Standards Manual (Mar 12, 2026)
chunk.unconfirmed: ticket life 30 vs 45 days: the official rule text with the 2026 change was not opened

chunk.title: Pennsylvania 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Pennsylvania's dig law is the Underground Utility Line Protection Law (Act 287 of 1974, as amended by Act 50 of 2017 and Act 127 of 2024), 73 P.S. 176 and after. The Public Utility Commission enforces it through its Damage Prevention Committee. One center: Pennsylvania One Call (PA 811). Notice: "not less than three nor more than ten business days in advance of beginning excavation." Complex projects: at least ten business days. The law gives no number of days a ticket lasts. It says to call again if you leave the site for more than two business days (unless you made other arrangements with the owners). Ticket life is not confirmed; go by PA One Call. Tolerance zone: within eighteen inches of the outside wall or edge of the line. Use prudent techniques there, such as hand-dug test holes or vacuum. Check the owners' responses (KARL) before digging. If an owner fails to respond you may proceed on the lawful start date, with due care. Hit a line: tell the owner right away; gas or liquid escaping, call 911.
chunk.source: 73 P.S. 176, 180, 182.10 (Underground Utility Line Protection Law; FindLaw copy, current as of Jan 1, 2026)

chunk.title: Rhode Island 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Dig Safe)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Rhode Island uses Dig Safe as its one-call center (call 811); the Division of Public Utilities and Carriers enforces the state's Dig Safe law. Pre-mark the dig area in white (paint, flags, stakes or whiskers), then call at least 72 hours ahead, not counting weekends and holidays, and not more than 30 days ahead. Ticket life: "tickets do not expire provided that the marks are maintained." In every Dig Safe state a ticket expires if digging does not start within 30 days. Renew with at least 72 hours' notice (weekends and holidays not counted) so there is no gap; if the scope of work changes, get a new ticket instead. Whether a renewal prints a new number is not confirmed. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 18 inches on each side. Hand dig or use vacuum equipment there; no machines until the line is verified. Power equipment may remove pavement only to the depth of the pavement. Dig Safe only notifies its members. Call non-member owners (often town water and sewer) yourself.
chunk.source: Dig Safe Excavator Manual (version Aug 2025; laws table updated 6/5/25) pp. 4-5, 9, 11, 14-19, 25-27, 31

chunk.title: South Carolina 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (SC811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: South Carolina's dig law is the Underground Facility Damage Prevention Act, S.C. Code Title 58, Chapter 36. One center: SC811. Wait: operators "have three full working days to mark," not counting the day you call. A normal request is good for 15 working days from its start time. Send an Extension any time before it runs out; an Extension does not refresh the paint. Marks gone: send a Remark, which makes a new ticket with a new number and gives operators three full working days. Once a request has expired you need a new one. Pre-mark in white paint, flags or stakes when the site can't be clearly identified. Before digging, verify that every operator has answered in Positive Response. No answer and no sign of a line: you may proceed. Signs of a line: request a No Show; the operator has three hours. Tolerance zone: 24 inches on either side of the mark plus half the diameter if known. No machines there until you can see the line; machines may remove pavement only. Hit a line: notify SC811 and the operator right away; danger or a release, call 911 first.
chunk.source: SC811 Excavator Manual 2026 pp. 9-23, 27-35; S.C. Code 58-36-10 to 58-36-120

chunk.title: South Dakota 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (South Dakota 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: South Dakota's dig law is SDCL chapter 49-7A, with the One-Call Notification Board writing the rules. One center: South Dakota 811. Notice (49-7A-5, 2026 Senate Bill 9): "at least forty-eight hours prior to the commencement of the excavation." The 48 hours start at 12:01 a.m. the day after you send the notice and skip Saturdays, Sundays and state legal holidays. Operators mark within "eighteen inches horizontally from the exterior sides of the underground facilities." Keep "a minimum horizontal clearance of eighteen inches" between the marked line and the cutting edge of any machine. If you must dig closer than 18 inches, expose the line first with hand tools or an approved noninvasive method, then protect and support it before using the machine again. How long a ticket lasts, the damage steps and the fine amounts were not in the text read and are not confirmed here: go by the ticket and South Dakota 811.
chunk.source: SDCL 49-7A-5 and 49-7A-8 as amended by 2026 Senate Bill 9 (enrolled)
chunk.unconfirmed: ticket life, damage steps, fine amounts

chunk.title: Tennessee 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Tennessee 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Tennessee's dig law is the Underground Utility Damage Prevention Act, T.C.A. 65-31-101 and after, with an Enforcement Board at the Tennessee Public Utility Commission. One center: Tennessee 811. Notice: "at least three (3) working days prior to the actual date of excavation" and not more than ten full working days ahead. A ticket is good for "fifteen (15) calendar days from the actual date specified to start." To keep digging, give a new notice at least three working days before the fifteenth day runs out; Tennessee 811 says you are then "given a new ticket number." When the digging is done, stop updating. Mark the dig area "with white paint, or by electronic white lining" unless an exception applies (for example the ticket gives a precise location). A property owner using non-mechanized tools on their own property is exempt. Within 100 feet of the edge of a street or highway, if an operator fails to locate in time the excavator is authorized to proceed. The tolerance zone (24 inches in 65-31-108) and penalty amounts were not re-read today and are not confirmed here.
chunk.source: T.C.A. 65-31-106 (FindLaw copy, current as of Jan 2, 2024); Tennessee 811 law page and FAQ
chunk.edition: FindLaw copy current as of January 2, 2024

chunk.title: Texas 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Texas811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Texas has two layers: Utilities Code chapter 251 (the one-call law for all lines) and Railroad Commission rule 16 TAC chapter 18 for pipelines (gas, hazardous liquid, CO2). Call 811 or use the Texas811 portal. Notice: at least 48 hours before digging, not counting weekends and legal holidays, and not more than 14 days ahead. Ticket life: 14 working days for pipeline locates unless you and the operator agree otherwise in writing. Not done: refresh the ticket for the area still to dig. Texas811 sends updates with a 2 business day notice. Tolerance zone for pipelines: half the pipe diameter plus at least 18 inches on each side. Wait for a positive response (marks, "all clear" or "no conflict"). None: give a second notice; if there is still none after 4 hours you may begin. Hit a pipeline: notify the operator through 811 within 1 hour, call 911 for a release, and file a damage report with the Railroad Commission within 30 days.
chunk.source: 16 TAC ch. 18 (Railroad Commission; sections as amended eff. Feb 12, 2018); Tex. Util. Code ch. 251
chunk.edition: 16 TAC ch. 18 as in effect Feb 12, 2018 (latest amendment shown)

chunk.title: Utah 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Blue Stakes of Utah 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Utah's dig law is Utah Code Title 54, Chapter 8a. One center: Blue Stakes of Utah 811. Notice: not "less than 48 hours before excavation begins" and not "more than 14 days before." The 48 hours count business days only; business hours are 8 AM to 4 PM, Monday to Friday, not holidays. A notice is "valid for 21 days from the day on which the notice is given." To keep going, renew at least 48 hours and no more than 7 calendar days before it expires. Blue Stakes gives an update a different ticket number. Tolerance zone: 24 inches on either side of the outside edge of the mark (or half the marked diameter plus 24 inches from the center). No power equipment inside the zone until you have found the exact location with hand tools. Operator did not mark or answer in 48 hours: file a no response notice; the operator then has 4 business hours. Hit a line: tell the operator right away; gas, electric or danger to life, call 911. No backfill until the operator says so.
chunk.edition: Utah Code as amended by the 2024 General Session (ch. 369)

chunk.title: Vermont 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Dig Safe)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Vermont uses Dig Safe as its one-call center (call 811); the Department of Public Service enforces the state's Dig Safe law. Pre-mark the dig area in white (paint, flags, stakes or whiskers), then call at least 72 hours ahead, not counting weekends and holidays, and not more than 30 days ahead. Ticket life: tickets expire 30 days from the day of issue. In every Dig Safe state a ticket expires if digging does not start within 30 days. Renew with at least 72 hours' notice (weekends and holidays not counted) so there is no gap; if the scope of work changes, get a new ticket instead. Whether a renewal prints a new number is not confirmed. Tolerance zone: the width of the line plus 18 inches on each side. Hand dig or use vacuum equipment there; no machines until the line is verified. Power equipment may remove pavement only to the depth of the pavement. Dig Safe only notifies its members. Call non-member owners (often town water and sewer) yourself.
chunk.source: Dig Safe Excavator Manual (version Aug 2025; laws table updated 6/5/25) pp. 4-5, 9, 11, 14-19, 25-27, 31

chunk.title: Virginia 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Virginia 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Virginia's dig law is the Underground Utility Damage Prevention Act, Va. Code 56-265.14 to 56-265.32, enforced by the State Corporation Commission. One center: Virginia 811. Wait: operators have 48 hours beginning at 7:00 a.m. the next working day after your locate request, so a Monday request is good Thursday at 7 AM. You may start sooner only when every operator has marked or posted a positive response that allows digging. A notice is "valid for 15 working days" from 7:00 a.m. the next working day after the request (or the scheduled date, if later). Three working days before it runs out, or when marks can't be read, request an update; Virginia 811 gives an update or re-mark a new request number. A re-mark is good for another 15 working days. Mark the site boundary in white paint, if practical, when you can't give an exact location. One request covers no more than one-third of a mile and only what can be dug in 15 working days. The hand-dig distance (2 feet in section 56-265.24) and fine amounts were not confirmed in this pass.
chunk.source: Va. Code 56-265.17 (2023 amendments); Virginia 811 "Ticket Types" sheet (May 15, 2026)

chunk.title: Washington 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Washington 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Washington's dig law is RCW 19.122, enforced by the Utilities and Transportation Commission (UTC). Mark the boundary of the dig "with white lining or, when necessary, white pin flags," then call 811. Notice: "not less than two full business days and not more than 10 full business days" before the work-to-begin date. Since January 1, 2026 you "may not commence excavation until the excavator has received positive response" from every operator with lines in the area. Marks expire 45 calendar days after you gave notice; to dig after that, give a new notice. Marks are accurate to within 24 inches of the outside of the line on both sides. Find the exact location before digging there: hand digging when practical, vacuum or air tools. Hit a line: tell the operator and 811, call 911 if it is an emergency, don't bury it, and report the damage to the UTC within 45 days.
chunk.edition: RCW as amended through Laws of 2025 chapter 292

chunk.title: West Virginia 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (West Virginia 811)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: West Virginia's dig law is W. Va. Code Chapter 24C. One center: West Virginia 811. Notice: "Not less than forty-eight hours, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and federal or state legal holidays," and not more than ten work days before work begins. Changing the start date or time: tell the one-call system at least 24 hours ahead, not counting weekends and holidays. The section sets no ticket life in days and no tolerance zone in inches; those are not confirmed here, so go by the ticket and West Virginia 811. Each equipment operator must be told to avoid damage, "including hand digging, when necessary," to keep a clearance "as may be reasonably necessary" from lines given the reach of the cutting edge, to protect marks and stakes, and to support lines during work and backfill. Line hit: report it immediately and give the operator reasonable time to repair. An emergency: alert the public and call 911. Damage that is not an emergency: notify the one-call system within 24 hours. Failing to notify or to report is a misdemeanor with a fine of "not more than $5,000," and you owe the repair cost.
chunk.source: W. Va. Code 24C-1-5 (code.wvlegislature.gov)
chunk.edition: W. Va. Code as posted Nov 20, 2026 (last act shown: 2006 SB 439)

chunk.title: Wisconsin 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (Diggers Hotline)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Wisconsin's dig law is Wis. Stat. 182.0175. One center: Diggers Hotline (811). A Public Service Commission panel hears complaints. Notice: "not less than 3 working days before the start of nonemergency excavation." Working days are days other than Saturday, Sunday and legal holidays. There is no set ticket life. Give a new notice if the dig does not start "within 10 days of the scheduled start date," if marks are destroyed or covered, or if work stops for more than 10 days. Keep "an estimated minimum clearance of 18 inches" between a marked, unexposed line and the cutting edge of the machine. Once the line is exposed the clearance can drop to twice the machine's limit of control or 12 inches, whichever is greater. Owners mark within 3 working days in the ANSI uniform colors. Before backfilling, inspect any line you exposed. If a line may be damaged, notify the owner immediately and do not backfill until it has been inspected. Gas or liquid that may endanger life: call 911. Emergency: take all reasonable precautions and notify owners as promptly as possible. Fine amounts were not confirmed.
chunk.source: Wis. Stat. 182.0175(1), (2), (2m), (3) (docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

chunk.title: Wyoming 811 rules in short: wait before you dig, how long a ticket is good, hand-dig zone (One-Call of Wyoming)
chunk.topic: 811 dig rules by state: wait before digging, ticket life, tolerance zone
chunk.text: Wyoming's dig law is the Wyoming Underground Facilities Notification Act, Wyo. Stat. 37-12-301 to 37-12-307. One center: One-Call of Wyoming (811). Notice: "at least two (2) full business days, but not more than fourteen (14) business days prior to any excavation." A job that runs longer than 14 business days needs the notice given again for each following 14 business day period. Mark the dig area before the locator comes, unless one operator can find the site from the address, there was a site meeting, or it is an emergency. Operators mark "within twenty-four (24) inches horizontally" of the outside of the line, in APWA colors, within two full business days. Reasonable care is always required, and it calls for hand or soft digging where needed to protect the line. Hit or touch a line: notify the operator and the center immediately. Gas or hazardous liquid released: call 911 first. Do not hide damage or repair it without authorization. In a dispute the excavator has to prove reasonable care. If the operator missed its deadline or marked wrong, an excavator who used reasonable care is not liable. Penalty amounts were not confirmed.
chunk.source: Wyo. Stat. 37-12-302 (Counsel Stack copy, 2026)

chunk.title: Michigan trench protection: its own rule, MIOSHA Part 9
chunk.topic: State safety plan: trench and excavation
chunk.text: Michigan does not use the federal excavation rule or OSHA's Type A, B and C soils. MIOSHA Construction Safety Standard Part 9, Excavation, Trenching and Shoring (R 408.40901 to R 408.40953, last amended effective January 3, 2024) says: "The side of an excavation more than 5 feet deep shall be sloped as prescribed in table 1, unless supported as prescribed in this part" (R 408.40941(1)). A shallower excavation is protected too "when examination of the ground indicates hazardous earth movement may be expected" (R 408.40941(2)). Support systems are designed by a qualified person and the design is kept at the jobsite (R 408.40942(2)). "Protective systems for use in excavations more than 20 feet in depth must be designed by a registered professional engineer" (R 408.40942(8)). An ongoing inspection by a competent person is required, and after every rainstorm (R 408.40932(4)). Federal OSHA starts at 5 ft or more (29 CFR 1926.652); this state's rule starts above 5 ft and uses its own table. Rule text read by an earlier check on 2026-11-20.

chunk.title: Oregon confined space rule (OAR 437-002-0146): what differs on the permit
chunk.topic: State safety plan: confined space
chunk.text: Oregon uses one confined space rule for general industry and construction, OAR 437-002-0146; Subdivision AA of its construction rules is reserved. As read on November 19, 2026: the permit must carry "The signature of the original supervisor authorizing entry" ((6)(b)(I)), a signature and not initials; "The date, start, and stop times" ((6)(b)(C)); and "Any problems, if any, encountered during the entry" as a permit item ((6)(b)(P)). Entrants get access to the completed permit before entry ((5)(e)). Cancelled permits are kept 1 year ((13)). Excavation and underground construction work is excluded, except entry into sanitary sewers large enough to enter ((2)). The federal construction rule allows the supervisor's signature or initials (29 CFR 1926.1206(g)). On an Oregon job, print the app's permit and have the supervisor sign it. The rule was not re-read on 2026-11-20.

chunk.title: Washington confined space rule (chapter 296-809 WAC)
chunk.topic: State safety plan: confined space
chunk.text: Washington has one confined space rule for all industries, chapter 296-809 WAC, instead of adopting the federal construction rule. As read on November 19, 2026: the permit carries the same 15 items as the federal general industry list, in a different order (WAC 296-809-50004), and the testing-equipment item names equipment able to detect a rise in atmospheric hazard if ventilation stops, which is federal construction item (e). The permit is available at entry (296-809-50002(5)), problems met during entry are noted on it (50002(7)), and it is kept 1 year (50006(2)). Air is tested with a calibrated, direct-reading instrument (296-809-60004(3)(a)). OSHA's adoption table lists this state's rule as different from the federal construction rule but at least as effective. The app's permit form covers these items. The chapter was not re-read on 2026-11-20.

Federal OSHA requires a protective system (sloping, benching, shoring or a shield) in an excavation 5 ft or deeper unless it is entirely in stable rock, and in a shallower one when the competent person sees a cave-in hazard (29 CFR 1926.652). Twenty-one states run their own OSHA plan for private construction crews; a plan must be at least as protective as federal and may be stricter, so on those jobs cite the state rule. What has been checked against the state's own rule text so far (as of 2026-11-20): Washington requires protection at 4 ft and, since June 1, 2026, a written trench work plan and a competent person on site during trench work; California keeps 5 ft and adds a Cal/OSHA permit for excavations 5 ft or deeper that people enter; Michigan uses its own Part 9 (slope or support over 5 ft, with its own angle table); Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon and Utah adopt the federal excavation standard, so 5 ft; Alaska, Kentucky, Minnesota and Tennessee adopt the federal rule and Hawaii, North Carolina and Virginia list no excavation rule of their own (from OSHA's and the agencies' pages, not each state code read line by line), so 5 ft; South Carolina uses the federal text and adds training to the competent person definition.
